name: Post Bridge
tagline: Schedule and cross-post to every major social network from one place, with an API and MCP server

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Creator (most popular) $29/month for 15 connected accounts, Growth $49 for 50, Pro $99 for unlimited. 7-day free trial on all tiers, annual gives 1 month free.
pricing.freeTier: No free plan, just a 7-day trial on every tier.

tiers.name: Creator
tiers.limits: Up to 15 connected social accounts; 100 uploads/posts per hour; 7-day trial.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited connected social accounts; 100 uploads/posts per hour; 7-day trial.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 7-day trial on paid plans
pricing.hiddenCosts: The service caps uploads/posts at 100 per hour and says it is not designed for thousands per day. API/MCP access may be separately priced or gated, but no current numeric add-on price was public; there is no official multi-user team mode.

verdictSummary: The core loop (compose, queue, cron tick, publish) is one-shottable for networks with open APIs like Bluesky, Mastodon, and Telegram. What you cannot one-shot is the reason Post Bridge exists: one-click posting to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, Threads, Pinterest, LinkedIn, and Google Business Profile. Those APIs are approval-gated behind Meta App Review, TikTok's Content Posting API, YouTube quota, and business verification, which as an individual you often can't even qualify for. On top of that sits per-platform video transcoding, constant token-refresh babysitting, and an API plus MCP server so an agent can post for you. You can vibecode a personal cross-poster for the open networks in a sitting; you cannot vibecode the approvals.
coreLoopDIY: Compose posts into a slot-based queue, publish on schedule to open-API networks via per-network adapters, and log outcomes, with a push-to-post-by-hand fallback for the approval-gated platforms.
whatYouLose: one-click connect to approval-gated platforms (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, Threads, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Google Business Profile)
pre-approved platform OAuth apps you often can't obtain as an individual
per-platform video transcoding and format handling
token-refresh babysitting as platforms expire and change policies
the hosted API and MCP server that lets a coding agent post for you
whyPeopleStillPay: The hosted product ships with OAuth apps that Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, and Google have already put through business verification and app review, so connecting Instagram or TikTok is a click instead of a multi-week developer-app process you may not qualify for solo. It also absorbs constant API and policy churn, per-platform video specs, and token expiry, and exposes an API plus MCP server so your coding agent can schedule posts through it rather than you rebuilding and maintaining the poster yourself.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social scheduler, self-hostable, covers much of the DIY core for open-API networks.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: Broad publishing, REST, MCP and hosted-free convenience; the closest answer that does not hand you a database.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: BrightBean does not document the same exact network coverage or managed API/MCP reliability guarantees as Post Bridge.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: Twenty-eight-plus channels, API, MCP and CLI; broad coverage bought with a broad deployment stack.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz's broad API and MCP coverage comes with PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, storage and social credentials to operate.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

alternatives.name: TryPost
alternatives.desc: Twelve-network cross-posting with REST and MCP; operate the server and bring your own platform credentials.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or production Docker Compose; a bare-metal installation is also documented.
facts.engines: AI writing can use OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the deployment template also exposes Anthropic and Gemini keys.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL or MySQL stores app data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media is local or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: TryPost covers twelve networks rather than every major Post Bridge destination and makes you run the API, jobs and storage yourself.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs a SQL database, Redis, media storage, and separate developer credentials for each social platform.

notes: The full big-platform set is the moat: the approvals, not the code · plus an API and MCP server so your agent posts for you instead of rebuilding it.
prompt:
Build me a personal social post scheduler to replace Post Bridge. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3; a localhost page with a compose box,
  image/video attach, and the queue ordered by send time.
- Targets with open APIs only: Bluesky (app password via @atproto/api),
  Mastodon (access token), and a Telegram channel (bot token). Creds in
  .env, one small adapter file per network so a fourth is addable later.
- For the approval-gated platforms people actually want (TikTok, Instagram,
  YouTube, Facebook, Threads, Pinterest, LinkedIn), do NOT fight their APIs:
  at post time send me an ntfy.sh push with the caption and media path so I
  can post by hand in a minute. Say clearly in the README that these need
  approved developer apps and business verification you cannot one-shot.
- Slot-based queue: I define posting times per weekday in my timezone and
  new posts fill the next free slot; a post can also be pinned to an exact
  datetime or duplicated across networks with per-network text and counts.
- A node-cron tick every minute publishes due posts, marks each row sent or
  failed, retries failures 3 times with backoff, and marks before sending so
  nothing double-posts.
- Attached media stored in media/ next to the database, images resized per
  network with sharp.
- A history page of the last 100 sent posts linking to the live posts.
- Runs on my always-on box; localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: cross-network analytics, teams, and per-platform video
  transcoding.
- README: getting a Bluesky app password, a Mastodon token, and a Telegram
  bot token, plus an honest note that social APIs drift and this needs
  occasional patching.
